newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- FEB 28.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Capital Market Commission President Stavros Thomadakis's comments on Wednesday provoked panic and a free fall of prices rather than the orderly correction wished for at the Athens Stock Exchange. The general price index recorded one of its biggest plunges, down 5.95 percent at closing and reaching the record level of 7.15 percent during the session, with almost all shares at the limit down.

--The union of bank employees said yesterday there were margins for a further reduction in interest rates for state-run banks as modernisation of operations would lead to a reduction of operating costs

--Calls for calm on the ASE following Thomadakis's apparently uncalculated statements; some, however, believe his statements came with the aim of turning the public confidence to the state's issue of treasury bills today with reduced interest of 10.5 percent.
--AFMs, tax file numbers, will be changed from the current eight digits to ten. The two new numbers will be related to date of birth.

--The National Housing Bank yesterday decided to reschedule debts owed by hotel enterprises. The bank has announced profits of 43.5 billion drachmas, dividends of 900 drachmas and one new share for each five old for shareholders.
--Estimates put February inflation at 6.5-6.6 percent, down from 6.8 percent the previous month.
--National economy ministry sources say that the government hoped for a continuation of the ASE's rise, considering it a factor for growth.
--The national economy ministry has ordered a new study on those groups facing economic and social problems. It is thought that a package of measures will be developed to assist these groups.
--Declarations must be submitted by the end of March for the first phase of the National Land Register programme.
--A new series of taxation breaks and investment incentives for new farmers are included in the agriculture ministry's bill, soon to be discussed in Parliament.
--The new trading hours will be the focus of discussions today at the national economy ministry with the presence of National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou.

--The fluctuations on the bourse have revealed operating and institutional problems and disagreements between the Capital Market Commission and brokers. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
